prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: rear-end collision in Sugar Land, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported knee injury. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1158; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Driver 1 was stopped in the right lane of the eastbound frontage road near a signalized intersection in Sugar Land, Texas, when the vehicle behind them, operated by Driver 2, failed to stop and struck the rear bumper at a speed that was clearly more than a light tap. Driver 1 was the operator of the vehicle and was seated behind the wheel at the time of impact. A Passenger was also in the front seat. Both occupants reported that Driver 1 struck the dashboard area with the left knee during the collision, and Driver 1 later complained of pain at the scene. Driver 2 acknowledged that they had looked down at a phone just before the impact and admitted fault. Two independent witnesses in a nearby vehicle and a pedestrian at the corner each described the sequence in the same way, and photographs taken at the scene show crushed rear body panels on Driver 2's vehicle and a matching crease in Driver 1's rear bumper. Responding officers found no prior damage or repair marks on either vehicle. Driver 1 is listed as the named insured on the policy covering the struck vehicle. Both vehicles were towed from the scene, and Driver 1 was transported by ambulance for evaluation.
